title: Examine an inherited norm through a respectful comparison

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A norm has a setting, purpose and participants who may differ. Compare an attributed account with your interpretation; neither a fictional household nor one real speaker represents an entire culture. For a live source choose a named or clearly situated voluntary first-person account, identify its audience/date and avoid treating outsider summaries as universal rules.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Two original fictional first-person accounts. Ren: “At our weekly family table, I often decline the first offer so the host can keep enough. The host usually offers again, but visitors may answer directly.” Sol: “In my shared household we ask once and take the answer literally because repeated offers feel pressuring. We tell new guests this before the meal.” Neither names a nation, religion or ethnicity.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare the same offer under both stated settings. Represent each reason, one shared concern and one limit on generalization. Keep this constructed comparison separate from an actual cultural encounter.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A guest says no after the host explicitly explains that offers are made once. May the host assume hidden assent because a different household uses repeated offers?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Ren’s account manages perceived scarcity; Sol’s manages pressure and clarity. Both can concern care for others while producing different conduct. A visitor should use the actual host’s stated meaning rather than infer refusal is insincere. Partial: state the different rules without reasons. Incorrect: conclude an entire culture always refuses or always pressures. Next consult an accessible situated first-person account and check whether it changes the constructed comparison.
criteria: Accounts remain attributed to their settings
A shared concern does not erase a real difference

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Respect the stated local meaning and actual answer. Ask a neutral clarification only if appropriate; do not let a cultural generalization erase the person’s choice.
